description: Tin is a chemical element with symbol Sn and atomic number 50. It is a soft, metallic-gray post-transition metal in group 14 of the periodic table that is soft enough to be cut with little force and can be bent by hand with little effort.
uses: Tin is used in many alloys including bronze, pewter, and tin-lead soft solders. It is used in the manufacture of transparent, electrically conducting films of indium tin oxide in optoelectronic applications, and is widely used for corrosion-resistant tin plating of steel, particularly for food packaging in tin cans. Tin-plated steel is preferred because of the low toxicity of inorganic tin.
characteristics: Tin is soft, malleable, ductile, and highly crystalline with a silvery-white color. When bent, a bar of tin produces a crackling sound called the tin cry from the twinning of crystals. It melts at about 232°C and boils at 2,602°C. Tin has two main allotropes: β-tin (white tin), which is stable at room temperature and malleable, and α-tin (gray tin), which is stable below 13.2°C and brittle with a diamond cubic structure. Metallic tin does not easily oxidize in air or water.
